comparator.name: Frisian Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The Frisian Language and Culture track is part of Groningen’s Dutch Languages and Cultures bachelor. This plan follows the September 2026 entry cohort. It combines Frisian studies, shared linguistics and literature, and a third-year minor, thesis and internship.

components.name: Bachelor's Thesis — Frisian Language and Culture
components.note: The thesis follows Research Approaches and the credit requirements in the regulations. It is normally written in the language of the track.

components.name: Internship — Frisian Language and Culture
components.note: Apply what you have learned in a Frisian language or cultural setting.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target explicitly names the Frisian Language and Culture route. The 2026-2027 TER recognizes this as the FTC track within BA Nederlandse Talen en Culturen and defines its separate course pathway, language outcomes, thesis language and field-specific second- and third-year requirements. The exact route is therefore selected independently of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three options develop distinct parts of the evidence: language and public communication, cultural interpretation, and heritage and political institutions. These related fields do not supply Frisian proficiency or the specialised regional curriculum. A fourth, Frisian-specific option fails on academic content.

notes.text: Groningen studies Frisian language, literature and culture within a dedicated track. The UCR options explore related questions through language and society, cultural interpretation, or heritage and public institutions.

UCR offers introductory Dutch and courses on language and literature. The illustrated options lack Frisian language study, a sequence in Frisian literature and history, and the Groningen track’s required internship and thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen’s Frisian Language and Culture track studies Frisian language, literature and society. It combines literary and linguistic study with an internship and a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options explore related questions about language, cultural identity or public heritage. Groningen builds these questions around Frisian language and regional study.

cellNotes.text: Both study language acquisition and use evidence to investigate it. UCR focuses on psychological and neurological processes.
